claims.claim: The Cardiff Giant was a ten-foot stone man found in a well trench
claims.quote: It was a 10-foot-tall (3.0 m), roughly 3,000 pound purported "petrified man", uncovered on October 16, 1869, by workers digging a well behind the barn of William C. "Stub" Newell, in Cardiff, New York.

claims.claim: The discovery took place in Cardiff, New York, on October 16, 1869
claims.quote: uncovered on October 16, 1869, by workers digging a well behind the barn of William C. "Stub" Newell, in Cardiff, New York

claims.claim: The photograph of the giant is by Bain News Service, 1910, public domain
claims.quote:
Date: 1910
Author: Bain News Service, publisher
Licence: Public domain

claims.claim: Two men hired to dig a well found the giant
claims.quote: Newell hired Gideon Emmons and Henry Nichols, ostensibly to dig a well, and on October 16, 1869, they found the giant.

claims.claim: The two men were Gideon Emmons and Henry Nichols, digging behind William Newell's barn
claims.quote: Newell hired Gideon Emmons and Henry Nichols, ostensibly to dig a well, and on October 16, 1869, they found the giant.

claims.claim: One of the diggers reportedly said, "I declare, some old Indian has been buried here!"
claims.quote: One of the men reportedly exclaimed, "I declare, some old Indian has been buried here!"

claims.claim: It was sold/presented as a petrified man, ten feet long
claims.quote: It was a 10-foot-tall (3.0 m), roughly 3,000 pound purported "petrified man"

claims.claim: Newell put up a tent and charged fifty cents for a fifteen-minute viewing
claims.quote: The next day, a tent was set up on the discovery site and Newell charged each visitor fifty cents for a fifteen-minute session of viewing the giant.

claims.claim: Three to five hundred people came each day
claims.quote: The number of visitors went to about three to five hundred per day as the demand for wagons and carriages dramatically increased.

claims.claim: Printed sheets listed its dimensions, with whole length 10 feet 4½ inches
claims.quote: ITS DIMENSIONS ARE / Whole length of the figure, 10 feet, 4½ inches (printed on the lithograph "THE ONONDAGA GIANT")

claims.claim: The lithograph is titled "The Onondaga Giant" and credited to Popular Graphic Arts
claims.quote: Archive title: File:The Onondaga giant LCCN2003666806.jpg ... Author: Popular Graphic Arts

claims.claim: The stone came from an Iowa gypsum quarry
claims.quote: This is the Gypsum Quarry from which was taken the block out of which the original "Cardiff Giant" was carved.

claims.claim: In 1868 George Hull hired men at Fort Dodge to quarry a block of gypsum ten feet four and a half inches long
claims.quote: In 1868, Hull, accompanied by a man named H. B. Martin, hired men to quarry out a 10-foot-4.5-inch-long (3.2 m) block of gypsum in Fort Dodge, Iowa

claims.claim: Hull told the quarrymen the block was intended for a monument to Abraham Lincoln in New York
claims.quote: telling them it was intended for a monument to Abraham Lincoln in New York

claims.claim: The stereocard view of Cardiff Glen, Fort Dodge, dates from 1873 and is an NYPL scan
claims.quote:
Description: View in Cardiff Glen, near Fort Dodge, Iowa.
Date: 1873
Author: Scan by NYPL

claims.claim: The giant was carved in Chicago
claims.quote: He shipped the block to Edward Burkhardt in Chicago, a German stonecutter. Burkhardt hired two sculptors named Henry Salle and Fred Mohrmann to create the giant.

claims.claim: It was buried for about a year before being found
claims.quote: On a night in late November 1868, the giant was buried in a hole in Newell's farm. Nearly a year later, Newell hired Gideon Emmons and Henry Nichols, ostensibly to dig a well, and on October 16, 1869, they found the giant.

claims.claim: Sculptors worked behind hung quilts to muffle the sound of carving
claims.quote: it is reported that they took steps to cover up their work during the carving, putting up quilts to lessen the sound of carving

claims.claim: Hull aged the surface with sand, sulphuric acid, and steel knitting needles set in a board to fake skin pores
claims.quote: In order for the giant to look ancient, Hull first wiped the giant using a sponge soaked with sand and water. The giant's surface was beaten with steel knitting needles embedded in a board to simulate pores. The giant was also rubbed with sulphuric acid to create a deeper, vintage-like color.

claims.claim: The hoax cost $2,600
claims.quote: By then, he had spent US$2,600 (equivalent to $63,000 in 2025) for the hoax.

claims.claim: Hull confessed on December 10, 1869
claims.quote: On December 10, 1869, Hull confessed everything to the press

claims.claim: On February 2, 1870, a court declared both Hull's giant and Barnum's plaster copy fakes
claims.quote: on February 2, 1870, both giants were revealed as fakes in court; the judge also ruled that Barnum could not be sued for terming a fake giant a fake

claims.claim: Barnum's copy was a plaster copy
claims.quote: he hired a man to model the giant's shape covertly in wax and create a plaster copy

claims.claim: Whether the Chicago stonecutter Edward Burkhardt knew what he was making is not clear
claims.quote: While it is not clear if Burkhardt was aware of Hull's intentions

claims.claim: The figure weighed nearly 3,000 pounds
claims.quote: The length of the giant was 10 feet 4+1⁄2 inches (3.162 m) and it weighed 2,990 pounds (1,360 kg).

claims.claim: Cardiff's hotels and restaurants had never been so busy
claims.quote: The hotels and restaurants in Cardiff saw more customers in those four days than they had ever seen before.

claims.claim: George Hull was a tobacconist
claims.quote: The giant was the creation of a New York tobacconist named George Hull.

claims.claim: The giant was buried on Hull's cousin's farm
claims.quote: During November 1868, Hull transported the giant by railroad to the farm of his cousin, William Newell.

claims.claim: Hull acted after losing an argument at a Methodist revival about the giants in Genesis 6:4
claims.quote: Hull got into an argument with Reverend Turk and his supporters at a Methodist revival meeting about Genesis 6:4, which states that there were giants who once lived on Earth. Hull, a skeptic, being the minority party, lost the argument.

claims.claim: Hull wanted the hoax to be exposed / "the man who made it wanted you to find out"
claims.quote: confessed proudly that he intended for the hoax to be exposed to reveal the tendency of the Christian community to believe in things too easily
